extracted.intended_audience: card issuers, compliance officers, legal counsel, and industry stakeholders participating in CFPB rulemaking or implementing Regulation Z (TILA) fee provisions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and final-rule criteria for setting and evaluating credit-card penalty fees (especially late fees) under Regulation Z/TILA, including safe-harbors, cost-analysis rules, excluded costs, and commentary examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reevaluation requirement for cost-based penalty fees
rubrics_metrics.description: A card issuer that uses the cost analysis provisions in §1026.52(b)(1)(i) must reevaluate its determination of whether a fee represents a reasonable proportion of total costs incurred at least once every 12 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 1026.52(b)(1)(i) further provides certain other requirements and conditions that apply if, as a result of the reevaluation, the card issuer determines that either a lower or higher fee represents a reasonable proportion of the total costs incurred. (Emphasizes periodic review and adjustment when cost determinations change.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs that may be considered under the cost analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment 52(b)(1)(i)-1 provides that card issuers may include in the costs for determining a penalty fee 'the costs incurred . . . as a result of [the] violation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cost analysis is intended to capture costs directly resulting from the omission or violation (i.e., the cost of a late payment), not unrelated costs. The CFPB solicited comment on whether additional clarifications were needed for how to perform a cost analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of 'losses and associated costs' from costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment 52(b)(1)(i)-2 states that 'losses and associated costs' (including the cost of holding reserves against potential losses and the cost of funding delinquent accounts) cannot be considered as costs incurred by a card issuer for purposes of §1026.52(b)(1)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board's 2010 Final Rule gave these examples; they are not exhaustive, but they make clear that certain loss-related items are excluded from what may be recovered through penalty fees to avoid shifting losses into penalty fees rather than upfront rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit exclusion of post-charge-off collection costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendment clarifies that any collection costs incurred after an account has been charged off in accordance with loan-loss provisions are not considered costs incurred for purposes of §1026.52(b)(1)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: post-charge-off activities are related to mitigating a loss rather than the cost of the late-payment violation; including them would require other consumers (who were merely delinquent) to subsidize losses arising from written-off accounts. CFPB adopts amendment for both Larger and Smaller Card Issuers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalty fees must be 'reasonable and proportional' to the omission or violation
rubrics_metrics.description: TILA requires that the amount of any penalty fee, including any late payment fee, be 'reasonable and proportional' to any omission with respect to, or violation of, the cardholder agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory standard limits what costs may be considered and is the controlling lens for both safe harbor and cost-analysis approaches; illustrative examples are not determinative of reasonableness under cost analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe-harbor late fee amount (CFPB final rule application)
rubrics_metrics.description: CFPB adopted and clarified a discretionary $8 late-fee safe harbor amount applicable to the issuers to which it applies (clarified as applicable to card issuers other than Smaller Card Issuers, i.e., Larger Card Issuers as described).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule amends commentary and illustrative examples to reflect the $8 late fee safe harbor for Larger Card Issuers. Larger Card Issuers can still elect to use the cost-analysis provisions if the safe-harbor amount is insufficient to cover pre-charge-off collection costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historic/alternative safe-harbor amounts for penalty fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board's 2010 Final Rule established penalty fee safe-harbor amounts of $25 for the first violation and $35 for additional violations of the same type occurring within the same billing cycle or one of the next six billing cycles (and, in Regulation Z as implemented by CFPB proposals, other numeric safe-harbor equivalents were discussed: e.g., §1026.52(b)(1)(ii) referencing $30/$41 under CFPB's then-current text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB explained the Board's rationale for those amounts (considering current fee practices, other account types, state laws, UK OFT threshold, deterrence data, and limited issuer-submitted cost data). Under CFPB proposals, the $8 change would be specific to late fees while other penalty fees could remain governed by the prior safe-harbor amounts unless otherwise amended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special safe harbor for charge card accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: §1026.52(b)(1)(ii)(C) provides a special safe harbor: when a charge card account that requires payment in full becomes seriously delinquent (not received required payment for two or more consecutive billing cycles), an issuer may impose a late fee not exceeding 3 percent of the delinquent balance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB recognized this is a form of late fee but did not propose to lower this special safe-harbor percentage; the proposed $8 safe harbor would not replace this special rule for qualifying charge card delinquencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: When higher fees for repeat violations are justified (deterrence/time window)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board reasoned that a higher safe-harbor amount for additional violations that occur during the same billing cycle or in one of the next six billing cycles is consistent with the deterrence factor, because imposition of a higher fee when multiple violations occur will have a significant deterrent effect on future violations for some consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board relied on evidence (e.g., a study showing consumers who incur a late fee are 40% less likely to incur a late payment the next month) and modeling submitted by commenters; however, it acknowledged data limitations and uncertainty about precise amounts needed for optimal deterrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer-conduct factor in setting fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Consumer conduct (e.g., multiple violations in a short period) is a statutory factor; multiple violations within a billing cycle or within the next six billing cycles may justify higher penalty fees because they indicate increased costs and credit risk and a more serious form of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board observed that consumers who pay late multiple times over six months generally present greater credit risk; CFPB noted the Board did not fully explain how additional costs would change credit risk and raised concerns about adding costs to consumers who cannot pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrative examples are not determinative
rubrics_metrics.description: The CFPB views illustrative examples in the commentary as neither representative nor determinative of a reasonable and proportional late fee amount determined pursuant to the cost-analysis provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB declined to lower illustrative example amounts to the $8 safe harbor because examples do not set the standard; they only illustrate application of the rule or commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot use penalty fees to subsidize other products or services
rubrics_metrics.description: In considering which costs should be considered for purposes of setting penalty fees, it would be inappropriate to consider penalty fees' subsidization of other products and services that card issuers may offer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB noted that the statutory requirement that fees be reasonable and proportional precludes considering broader issuer business objectives (like funding other services) when setting penalty fees under the cost-analysis approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuers' alternate recovery mechanisms exist (APR/upfront pricing)
rubrics_metrics.description: If safe-harbor amounts do not permit full recovery of certain costs (e.g., some losses), issuers have other mechanisms to recover costs such as adjusting APRs and other upfront pricing strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB cites risk-based pricing and periodic rates as the standard market means to account for losses, supporting exclusion of losses/post-charge-off costs from penalty-fee cost calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and non-exhaustive nature of 'loss' examples
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board's 2010 Final Rule examples of what constitutes a 'loss' (e.g., cost of holding reserves, cost of funding delinquent accounts) were not presented as exhaustive definitions of 'loss.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CFPB's amendment provides further clarification on what constitutes a 'loss' and reiterates that the purpose of excluding post-charge-off costs is to avoid linking late fees to costs not directly caused by the individual's late payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: CFPB may set different safe-harbor approaches (single amount, staggered fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: CFPB solicited comment on whether to set a different late-fee amount, retain higher safe-harbor amounts, or set a staggered late-fee structure (e.g., small dollar amounts charged every certain number of days until a cap).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is process guidance: CFPB sought data and rationale for alternatives, indicating that the rulemaking contemplates different safe-harbor designs and invites empirical justification.
